chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Faddal, who said: I heard a man ask Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

He said: I manage slaves and sell them, and people say it is not proper. He (al-Rida, peace be upon him) said to him: 'And what is wrong with it? All things that are sold are permissible if the servant fears Allah, Exalted and Mighty, in it, so there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: So there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is buying and selling slaves permissible in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) validates the pre-Islamic and early Islamic practice of slave trade by emphasizing that the permissibility of any commodity, including slaves, hinges on the owner's *taqwa* (God-consciousness) in managing the transaction and treating the slave with justice. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that the institution was not inherently abolished but regulated, serving as a transitional phase toward eventual emancipation through ethical conduct and manumission.
